scenario.description: A population health program director must assign the hospital's only newly available remote-monitoring kit to one of two recently discharged cardiac patients and finalize the monitoring, authorization, and caregiver-training plan, with input from cardiology, utilization review, and social work.

shared_context.S1: The hospital has one newly available cellular remote-monitoring kit and two recently discharged cardiac patients, Rowan and Ellis, being considered for it.
shared_context.S2: The kit can transmit blood-pressure and weight readings to the hospital's care team.
shared_context.S3: Elena makes the final assignment and signs the monitoring plan.
shared_context.S4: The program's routine is to check once with cardiology, utilization review, and social work for relevant information on the patients before finalizing; each specialist records any applicable order, authorization, or support arrangement in the meeting record, or confirms when their department has nothing further to add.

PF1.text: Dr. Shah's discharge order for Rowan requires the kit to begin at 08:00 tomorrow, with blood-pressure readings twice daily and weight readings once daily for exactly 14 days; Rowan has no functioning home monitor.

PF2.text: The payer approved Rowan's remote-monitoring service only through May 28 at 23:59, so the authorization end date in the plan must be exactly May 28 at 23:59.

PF3.text: Rowan's spouse can attend device training only tomorrow from 16:30 to 17:00 and needs a Vietnamese interpreter; Linh has confirmed that an interpreter can attend during that window.

acceptance_conditions: The remote-monitoring kit must be assigned to Rowan.
The plan must require two blood-pressure readings per day, one weight reading per day, and exactly 14 monitoring days.
The authorization end date must be May 28 at 23:59.
A caregiver-training commitment must schedule Rowan's spouse for tomorrow from 16:30 to 17:00.
A Vietnamese interpreter must be included in the caregiver-training commitment.
The clinical order requiring Rowan's monitoring plan must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C2: decisions['monitoring_start'] == '08:00 tomorrow' and decisions['blood_pressure_readings_per_day'] == 2 and decisions['weight_readings_per_day'] == 1 and decisions['monitoring_duration_days'] == 14
content_checks.C4: any(c['type'] in ['device_training', 'training_schedule'] and c['target'] in ['Rowan', "Rowan's spouse"] and '16:30' in c['detail'] and '17:00' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] in ['device_training', 'training_schedule'] and c['target'] in ['Rowan', "Rowan's spouse"] and 'Vietnamese' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The order changes the assignment from an open choice to Rowan and fixes the monitoring start, two daily blood-pressure readings, one daily weight reading, and exactly 14 days.
The payer record changes the authorization end field from an unresolved date to exactly May 28 at 23:59.
The caregiver arrangement changes the plan to a tomorrow 16:30-17:00 training commitment and adds a Vietnamese interpreter requirement.
